about: Seed data for src/data/landmarks.mjs (visitor brief item 2). Every entry cites its sources. ll is [lat, lng] in decimal degrees from the cited page; null means not found yet: fill it from OpenStreetMap and cite it. photo_key matches PHOTOS in src/site.mjs; null means no photo yet.

landmarks.name: First Christian Church
landmarks.access: Active congregation. Visiting arrangements not confirmed; view from outside.
landmarks.notes: Visit Columbus Indiana gives the NHL year as 2000; Wikipedia gives January 3, 2001. Confirm with the NPS NHL list before showing a date.

landmarks.name: North Christian Church (The LEX)
landmarks.architect: Eero Saarinen, completed by Kevin Roche; landscape by Dan Kiley; furnishings by Alexander Girard
landmarks.access: The church closed in July 2022. The Bartholomew County Public Library has owned it since 2024 as The LEX and is renovating it. General interior access not confirmed.

landmarks.name: Irwin Union Bank (Irwin Office Building)
landmarks.architect: Eero Saarinen; 1973 annex by Kevin Roche and John Dinkeloo; landscape by Dan Kiley
landmarks.access: Vacant since the pandemic and on the market, per The Republic. Not open to visitors.
landmarks.notes: Wikipedia gives 500 Washington Street; The Republic gives 525 Jackson St. for the Irwin Office Building at Fifth and Washington. A planned sale to Toyota Material Handling fell through. Recheck status before publishing.

landmarks.name: Cleo Rogers Memorial Library and Henry Moore's Large Arch
landmarks.architect: I. M. Pei; sculpture by Henry Moore
landmarks.access: Main library of the Bartholomew County Public Library, open during library hours. The Large Arch (1971) is outdoors.

landmarks.name: Bartholomew County Courthouse
landmarks.access: View from outside. Interior access not confirmed.
landmarks.notes: Listed on the National Register of Historic Places November 15, 1979.

landmarks.name: Columbus City Hall
landmarks.architect: Edward Charles Bassett, Skidmore, Owings & Merrill
landmarks.access: City offices. Public meetings in the City Council Chambers.

landmarks.name: Robert N. Stewart Bridge
landmarks.address: Carries Second Street (confirm the crossing and endpoints on OpenStreetMap)
landmarks.notes: Formerly the Second Street Bridge. Cable-stayed, with 40 cables in a fan. Colored lighting added in 2012; renamed for former mayor Robert N. Stewart in 2013.

landmarks.name: Miller House and Garden
landmarks.architect: Eero Saarinen; interiors by Alexander Girard; garden by Dan Kiley
landmarks.access: Tour only. The official tour departs from and returns to the Columbus Visitors Center; ages 10 and up; no other public access. Typically closed for maintenance in January and February.
landmarks.notes: Owned by the Indianapolis Museum of Art at Newfields. Don't send visitors to the house address.

landmarks.name: Fire Station 4
landmarks.architect: Robert Venturi (Venturi and Rauch), with Denise Scott Brown
landmarks.access: View from outside. Current use not confirmed.

landmarks.name: The Commons and Chaos I
landmarks.architect: Jean Tinguely (Chaos I, 1974); building rebuilt by Koetter Kim & Associates, 2011 (original by Cesar Pelli)
landmarks.address: Downtown, Washington Street (confirm the street number with The Commons)
landmarks.access: Enclosed public space owned by the city. Hours not confirmed.
landmarks.notes: Chaos I is owned by the Columbus Park and Recreation Department.

landmarks.name: First Baptist Church
landmarks.access: Church. Visiting arrangements not confirmed; view from outside.
landmarks.notes: Needs a credited photo before it appears in photo layouts.

landmarks.name: Mabel McDowell Adult Education Center
landmarks.access: A working BCSC adult education center. View from outside.
landmarks.notes: Wikipedia's two pages disagree on the NHL year (2001 and 2003). Confirm with the NPS NHL list.

landmarks.name: The Republic Newspaper Office
landmarks.access: Now IU's J. Irwin Miller Architecture Program. Visit Columbus Indiana says a public gallery is open to visitors.
landmarks.notes: Wikipedia gives October 16 and October 17, 2012 in different places. Glass walls once showed the presses to the street.
